title: Injective objects in the comma category of an exact left adjoint
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives: every object admits a monomorphism into an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $L:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive exact functor, meaning that it preserves short exact sequences, and suppose that $L$ has an additive right adjoint $R$. Define $\mathcal T_L$ to have objects $(P,N,u)$ with $P\in\mathcal A$, $N\in\mathcal B$, and $u:LP\to N$, and morphisms $(a,b):(P,N,u)\to(P',N',u')$ satisfying $b u=u' L(a)$. Addition and composition are componentwise. Then $\mathcal T_L$ is abelian, its kernels and cokernels are computed in the two components, and it has enough injectives. Both evaluation functors $e_0(P,N,u)=P$ and $e_1(P,N,u)=N$ are exact and send injective objects to injective objects. The functor $\Delta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal T_L$, $P\mapsto(P,LP,\operatorname{id}_{LP})$, $a\mapsto(a,L(a))$, is additive and exact.

source.place: Tag 015Z, lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives, supplies the adjoint/injective ingredient; the exact-comma construction is an agent auxiliary lemma for the relative cohomology assertion in ILO XVI, printed p.248. The construction and embedding argument are recorded in the delivery report, not asserted to be verbatim in Stacks.

proof.text: The morphism sets of $\mathcal T_L$ are subgroups of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(P,P')\oplus\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(N,N')$: the equation $bu=u'L(a)$ is additive because $L$ is additive. Composition is bilinear componentwise. The triple $(0,0,0)$ is a zero object (an additive functor sends a zero object to a zero object since $L(1_0)=L(0)=0$). For two triples take $(P_1\oplus P_2,N_1\oplus N_2,w)$, where $w=\sum_{j=1}^2\iota^N_j u_j L(\pi^P_j)$. Its componentwise inclusions and projections are morphisms of triples: for example $wL(\iota^P_j)=\iota^N_j u_j$, by the biproduct identities and additivity of $L$. They satisfy $\pi_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_j\iota_j\pi_j=1$ componentwise, giving a biproduct. Thus $\mathcal T_L$ is additive.

source.place: Tag 00ZY, definition-preadditive, and Tag 0109, definition-abelian-category; agent componentwise biproduct construction

proof.text: For $f=(a,b):(P,N,u)\to(P',N',u')$, choose kernels $k_a:K_a\to P$ and $k_b:K_b\to N$. Since $buL(k_a)=u'L(a k_a)=0$, there is a unique $w:LK_a\to K_b$ with $k_bw=uL(k_a)$. This makes $(K_a,K_b,w)\xrightarrow{(k_a,k_b)}(P,N,u)$ a morphism killed by $f$. If $(x,y):(S,T,v)\to(P,N,u)$ is killed by $f$, uniquely factor $x=k_a\bar x$, $y=k_b\bar y$. The equation $k_b\bar yv=yv=uL(x)=k_bwL(\bar x)$ implies $\bar yv=wL(\bar x)$ by the monicity of $k_b$; a kernel is monic directly by uniqueness in its universal property. Hence $(\bar x,\bar y)$ is the unique factorization in $\mathcal T_L$. This proves the componentwise kernel formula.

source.place: Tag 0106, definition-kernel; agent universal-property calculation for the comma kernel

proof.text: Choose cokernels $q_a:P'\to C_a$ and $q_b:N'\to C_b$. The functor $L$ preserves the cokernel of $a$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to the coequalizer of the parallel pair $(a,0)$, a diagram indexed by a finite, hence small, category; additivity gives $L(0)=0$. Since $q_bu'L(a)=q_bbu=0$, there is a unique $w:LC_a\to C_b$ with $wL(q_a)=q_bu'$. Thus $(q_a,q_b)$ is a morphism to $(C_a,C_b,w)$ and kills $f$. Given $(x,y):(P',N',u')\to(S,T,v)$ killed by $f$, uniquely write $x=\bar xq_a$ and $y=\bar yq_b$. Precomposing the desired relation $\bar yw=vL(\bar x)$ with $L(q_a)$ gives $yu'=vL(x)$, which holds. The map $L(q_a)$ is epic, being a cokernel, so the relation holds. The component factorizations are unique, proving that this is the cokernel in $\mathcal T_L$.

source.place: Tag 0106, definition-kernel, and Categories Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact (1); agent comma cokernel construction

proof.text: In a preadditive category with kernels, $f$ is monic exactly when its kernel object is zero: if $f$ is monic its kernel arrow is zero and monic, so the kernel identity is zero; conversely $fx=fy$ makes $x-y$ factor through the zero kernel, hence $x=y$. The argument for epimorphisms and zero cokernels is dual, using differences of maps out of the target. A triple is zero exactly when both components are zero, because its identity is zero exactly when both component identities are zero. Applying these observations to Steps 2 and 3 shows that $(a,b)$ is monic, respectively epic, exactly when both $a,b$ are monic, respectively epic.

source.place: Tag 0E43, lemma-kernel-mono, and Tag 010C, lemma-characterize-injective; agent difference-of-morphisms verification

proof.text: Every mono $a$ in either abelian component category is the kernel of its own cokernel $q_a$. Indeed, by [def-sp-abelian] it is a kernel of some $r$; write $r=hq_a$ since $ra=0$. Any $x$ with $q_ax=0$ then satisfies $rx=0$ and factors uniquely through $a$, as required. Dually an epi $a$ is the cokernel of its own kernel $k_a$: express $a$ as a cokernel of $s$, factor $s=k_at$ since $as=0$, and use the cokernel property of $s$ for any map killing $k_a$. By Step 4 a mono in $\mathcal T_L$ has monic components, so these component kernel properties and Step 2 make it the kernel of its componentwise cokernel from Step 3. Dually every epi is the cokernel of its kernel. Together with Steps 1–3, this verifies precisely the abelian-category axioms in [def-sp-abelian].

source.place: Tag 0109, definition-abelian-category; agent normal-mono and normal-epi verification from the defining axioms

proof.text: A sequence $0\to X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow g Z\to0$ of triples is short exact precisely when each component sequence is: in an abelian category this says that $f$ is a kernel of $g$ and $g$ a cokernel of $f$, and Steps 2–3 give these universal properties componentwise. For the reverse implication the unique component factorizations form a morphism of triples by the same cancellation calculations as in Steps 2–3. Consequently both additive evaluations $e_0,e_1$ preserve short exact sequences and are exact. For $\Delta$, the relation defining a morphism is $L(a)=L(a)$, and additivity is immediate. Applying $\Delta$ to a short exact sequence gives that sequence in component zero and its $L$-image in component one, both short exact by the hypothesis on $L$. The componentwise criterion therefore makes $\Delta$ additive and exact. Also $Z:\mathcal B\to\mathcal T_L$, $N\mapsto(0,N,0)$, is additive and exact by the same criterion.

source.place: Tag 010E, definition-exact (including short exact sequences); agent short-exactness test and graph/zero-section calculations, with exact meaning preservation of short exact sequences as in the item

proof.text: There are natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_L}(\Delta S,(P,N,u))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(S,P)$, sending $(a,b)$ to $a$ with inverse $a\mapsto(a,uL(a))$. Likewise $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_L}(Z T,(P,N,u))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(T,N)$ by $(0,b)\leftrightarrow b$. Thus $\Delta\dashv e_0$ and $Z\dashv e_1$. Both left adjoints are additive and exact by Step 6, and the categories are abelian by Step 5 and the hypotheses. Apply [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] to each of these adjunctions. It follows that $e_0$ and $e_1$ send injective triples to injective objects in their respective component categories.

source.place: Tag 015Z, lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives, implication (b) to (c); explicit adjunction bijections for the evaluations

proof.text: Write $\varepsilon:LR\to1_{\mathcal B}$ for the counit of the given adjunction. Define $r_0(I)=(I,0,0)$ and $r_1(J)=(RJ,J,\varepsilon_J)$; their actions on morphisms are $(c,0)$ and $(R(d),d)$, respectively. For a triple $X=(P,N,u)$, maps $X\to r_0(I)$ are precisely $(a,0)$ with arbitrary $a:P\to I$. Maps $X\to r_1(J)$ correspond to arbitrary $b:N\to J$: the first component is the adjoint transpose $\widehat{bu}:P\to RJ$, the unique map satisfying $\varepsilon_J L(\widehat{bu})=bu$. These natural bijections give $e_0\dashv r_0$ and $e_1\dashv r_1$. The displayed actions are additive since $R$ is additive. As $e_0,e_1$ are exact, [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] shows that $r_0(I)$ and $r_1(J)$ are injective whenever $I$ and $J$ are injective.

source.place: Tag 015Z, lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives; agent construction of the right adjoints of the evaluations

proof.text: For $X=(P,N,u)$ choose monomorphisms $i:P\hookrightarrow I$ and $j:N\hookrightarrow J$ with $I,J$ injective, using enough injectives in the two component categories. By Step 8 there are maps $X\to r_0(I)$ corresponding to $i$ and $X\to r_1(J)$ corresponding to $j$; their first components are $i$ and $\widehat{ju}$ and their second components are $0$ and $j$. Pair them to obtain $X\to r_0(I)\oplus r_1(J)$ with components $(i,\widehat{ju}):P\to I\oplus RJ$ and $j:N\to J$ (identifying $0\oplus J$ with $J$). The first component is monic because its composite with the projection to $I$ is $i$, and the second is monic by choice. Step 4 makes the map of triples monic. Finally this finite biproduct is injective: a map from the source of any mono to it has two component maps into $r_0(I),r_1(J)$; extend these separately using their injectivity and pair the extensions, obtaining an extension to the biproduct. This uses exactly the lifting definition [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Every triple therefore embeds in an injective triple, proving enough injectives.

source.place: Tag 0135, definition-injective, and Tag 0137, lemma-product-injectives; agent explicit embedding and two-factor extension argument
